The new findings relax the monotonicity condition of the constraints, allowing a larger class of feasible solutions, which includes when the constraints are preserved under decreasing functions.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactical information, as established in previous studies [Tenney et al., 2019, Jawahar et al., 2019, Hewitt and Manning, 2019]. This work presents two unsupervised constituent parsing models, UPOA and its enhanced version UPOA+, designed to leverage this capability. Both models utilize the self-attention mechanism to generate linear projection matrices for queries and keys, thereby achieving this goal. Moreover, the paper provides evidence that linear projection matrices can effectively capture phrase structure information, thereby enabling the models to excel in downstream tasks that rely on constituent parsing. Notably, the models were trained on the English language without any annotations, thereby validating their robustness in real-world applications. Experimental evaluations were conducted across various languages, including English, German, and Czech, with UPOA+ consistently outperforming other unsupervised models in English and significantly surpassing a supervised model in accuracy.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess the unique capability to distinguish between diverse objects within intricate environments by analyzing each pixel across various frequency ranges. Although HSI cameras are becoming increasingly accessible, associated algorithms have not been extensively utilized. This research delves into a novel application, specifically employing hyperspectral images for cityscape object segmentation using an unsupervised learning approach to circumvent the need for manual object classification. This method capitalizes on the rich spectral data inherent in HSI images, which facilitates efficient object segmentation within complex urban environments. By analyzing the inherent properties of HSI images and developing a corresponding segmentation framework, we demonstrate how these images can contribute to enhanced semantic segmentation in urban settings. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our proposed unsupervised segmentation technique, which yields satisfactory results with minimal computational demands.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267652's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which challenges our current understanding of internal rotation in these stars and prompts us to investigate alternative explanations, including the possibility of surface and interior processes that influence the rotation rate differently.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. Despite being widely adopted, the RAM model lacks a solid theoretical foundation, characterized by inconsistent definitions and a lack of cohesive results. This research aims to rectify this issue by developing a new RAM model with desirable algorithmic properties and robust complexity classes, particularly linear-time computability for problems like LIN and CONST-DELAY-lin, an enumeration class based on linear-time verification. To achieve this, several challenges were addressed, including the normalization of RAM computations, definition of hardware-independent algorithmic complexity, and construction of a powerful RAM algorithm for a problem previously only solved by a higher-level computation model. The newly developed RAM model has three fundamental properties: (i) efficient algorithmic complexity, (ii) distinct complexity classes for RAM computations of differing complexities, and (iii) a linear-time solution to a problem previously resolved through a higher-level computation model (specifically, CONST-DELAY-lin).

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new framework exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative approach in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by mapping invariant differential forms from the tropical Torelli map. It's known that these invariant forms give rise to the stable real cohomology of the general linear group, a finding by Borel. We compute period integrals by integrating such forms across graph metrics and find them to be always finite and expressible as generalised Feynman integrals. Our integrals have further application in identifying non-zero homology classes in the graph complex, providing novel perspectives on the cohomology structure and forging links between graph theory, motivic Galois groups and quantum field theory.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement.  This evidence confirms our hypothesis that auxiliary variables are utilized in object categorization, and highlights the importance of communication in recurrent neural networks.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains a significant obstacle in the analysis of one-dimensional systems. We have successfully demonstrated, however, that these correlations may be eliminated through an appropriate transformation, revealing the unique topological characteristics that arise as a result. In this study, we focus specifically on the correlated Haldane model and show that the symmetry-based topological classification is unaffected by the correlations when the system is Hermitian. Conversely, in the non-Hermitian domain, correlations introduce an additional topological characteristic, specifically the pseudo-Berry curvature, which is utilized to define a new type of topological characteristic. We have devised a topological invariant that effectively measures the pseudo-Berry curvature and has proven the susceptibility of the correlated Haldane model to correlations. Our findings thus broaden the scope of topological characteristics to encompass correlations, thereby enriching the topological framework of one-dimensional systems.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible in four-dimensional space if certain conditions are met concerning the sizes and their factorization. Additionally, in binary GCM quadruples, possible sizes are postulated as unlimited, which is confirmed for sizes 78x78 and a few scattered instances, whereas all positive integers below 1000 can be covered in a one-dimensional space of a quaternary GCM quad.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC and previously collected data from 7 and 8 TeV LHC, totaling 104.6 fb^-1. The findings from four-lepton final state analysis provide joint constraints on Higgs boson width and its interaction with electroweak vector bosons. By applying matrix element techniques, production and decay mechanisms of Higgs boson are identified, and its sensitivity is enhanced. The constraints on non-standard interactions with electroweak vector bosons are also explored, with the result showing compatibility with standard model predictions. Assuming standard model-like couplings, the Higgs boson width is constrained between 0.4 and 5.4 MeV, while the constraints on non-standard interactions range from -0.30 to -0.16% and from 0.16 to 0.30%.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within hyperspectral images, where each band must be analyzed simultaneously. This study breaks down the analysis into two distinct stages via a feature fusion deep convolutional autoencoder (FFDCAE), commencing with band selection using unsupervised techniques, followed by classification of the selected bands via a self-tuning convolutional neural network (STCNN). Utilizing remotely sensed images of Mt. Sinabung in Indonesia, both before and after the volcanic eruption, and using feature fusion techniques, EuroSDR is hosting a competition to demonstrate the effectiveness of various approaches. Following a comparative evaluation of different methods, it is determined that FFDCAE yields the highest accuracy of 100% in change detection of hyperspectral images, surpassing other participant methods.

We discover a novel linear relationship in the coefficients of $d(n, n+4; \mathbb{Z})$, specifically the sum of integers represented as the sum of squares $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_k^2$ with an additive complement $n$, which we find to be linearly related to the coefficients of $d(n, n+1; \mathbb{Z})$. As a result, the linear sum of the former coefficient series equals the quadratic sum of the latter, leading to an intriguing new relationship. Likewise, similar sums for $d(n, n+2; \mathbb{Z})$ and $d(n, n+3; \mathbb{Z})$ also exhibit linear relationships, though they are proportional to $d(n, n+1; \mathbb{Z})$. These relationships are unique to the circle packings of points with an odd number of points.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics, and it can rival Coulomb interactions to give rise to intricate phenomena.
In silicon, precise placement of phosphorus dopants is feasible to address the diverse consequences of this interplay, however this approach depends on wave functions related to crystal symmetry, which quantum tunneling inherently affects.
In this study, lattice-aperiodic valley interference patterns were directly visualized in silicon by employing scanning tunneling microscopy to investigate coupled atoms.
The findings demonstrate that valley selection rules can be violated due to the interplay of tunneling and Coulomb interactions, a phenomenon that can result in the emergence of unexpected spin-resonance characteristics.
This research reveals the unobtrusive impact of valley interference on the motion of electrons, thereby informing the precise control of quantum interactions in silicon-based systems, which is crucial for quantum computing and quantum communication applications.

Several disciplines have been influenced by optimization techniques in various real-world scenarios, hence their importance is being increasingly acknowledged by the community. As a result of this growing interest, researchers have been able to develop multiple open-source frameworks for optimization, ultimately contributing to innovation in both techniques and their practical applications. In the context of this study, we introduce a novel framework, known as LibOPT, for efficiently implementing and prototyping nature-inspired optimization algorithms. By integrating 15 established techniques and 112 benchmark functions, as well as supporting 11 novel hypercomplex-based approaches, our framework surpasses others in its domain, thus marking it as a groundbreaking innovation in optimization software development. Utilizing LibOPT under the C paradigm proves to be remarkably user-friendly and adaptable, as evidenced by the inclusion of clear source-code examples demonstrating the practical usage of the framework.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is simply transitive, the transitivity degree is infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, as well as proving a key theorem that allows for the determination of this degree for any smooth projective variety that has a simply transitive automorphism group.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our approach recognizes that for multi-particle states, the total system momentum is the only well-defined property. Calculating the total momentum involves non-commutative composition of individual particle momenta, which become ambiguous. Our results indicate that previous Fock space constructions were flawed due to incorrect assumptions and lack success. We demonstrate that momentum exchange underlies a relativistic covariance principle in the braiding of quantum numbers, solving a persistent challenge in the field.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide bandgap semiconductors. We utilize this technique to
investigate charge transport in scCVD diamond by exciting its charge carriers
with a femtosecond laser. Due to its two-photon nature, the technique confines
charge carrier generation in 3-D around the laser focal point, enabling us to
achieve a spatial resolution of approximately 5 micrometers. We generate a
significant electric field within a 10-nanometer thick Debye layer surrounding
diamond's surface, thereby facilitating charge transport studies under
experimentally controlled conditions. Our results are then compared with a 3-D
numerical model based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation, which
includes a numerical solution to the Poisson equation. We demonstrate the
capability to independently modify the semiconductor's carrier generation
position, temperature, and electric field to obtain in-depth insights into
diamond's charge transport properties.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. In this study, we report on the performance of our models in the inaugural Arabic Misogyny Identification challenge, where we evaluate three models that can learn multiple tasks simultaneously, alongside their individual-task counterparts. Our approach relies on the pre-trained MARBERT language model to analyze text inputs. Our results indicate that the proposed models achieved top-tier outcomes, securing first, second, and third place in both the misogyny identification and classification tasks.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when the environment model is imperfectly known. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates the connection between latent variable filtering and Gaussian Processes. This connection enables efficient computational handling of large-scale problems and highlights that model-based algorithms can achieve performance comparable to model-free methods while providing a guarantee of convergence to the optimal policy.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching approach seeks to mitigate network strain during peak wireless network times, whereas distributed computation explores the balance between computation and communication within a distributed system. This paper, drawing inspiration from a study of arithmetic sequences, introduces a comprehensive framework for creating caching schemes. This framework enables efficient caching of numerous files by generalizing prior research in the caching field. Furthermore, the framework has been successfully applied to situations where file caching is subject to constraints in terms of cost, storage, and confidentiality.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad from topos theory, which has been adapted for univalent type theory by Escard\'o and Knapp. Our work confirms that using the lifting monad provides a viable way to handle partiality within univalent type theory, and we also demonstrate that a predicative and constructive Scott model is achievable. Notably, we avoid reliance on choice or quotient inductive-inductive types, unlike other approaches to dealing with partiality.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's spatial structure and movement patterns.
In this study, a novel control approach for a prism-shaped robotic arm is presented, enabling safe navigation through a 2D environment with unexpected or moving obstacles.
A control strategy that prioritizes optimality and safety has been developed, which ensures the robot maintains a safe distance from obstacles while moving, although this approach may result in sub-optimal performance due to its conservative nature.
Consequently, a real-time collision avoidance algorithm based on the Global Planned Path is proposed to accelerate the robot's movement and overcome obstruction-related speed limitations.
Additionally, a dynamic memory scheme is introduced to optimize the response time and efficiency of the system.
As a result, this control framework allows the prism-shaped robotic arm to successfully navigate through a sequence of tests featuring stationary and moving obstacles.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on complex descriptions, often through quantum field theory or nonlinear differential equations. These descriptions sometimes conflict with key principles in interferometry and information processing. Nevertheless, a possibility of compatibility remains, and we provide a solid foundation for quantum operations, derived from solving evolution equations, and build upon this base with control techniques and efficient state sampling methods to develop practical nonlinear gates, especially a nonlinear Hadamard gate. Furthermore, our work in BEC interferometry and quantum computing redefines the paradigm by incorporating principles from nonlinear quantum mechanics, effectively applying it to interferometry and information processing.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications for capturing nonlinear geometric attributes. To obtain a solution set devoid of degeneration, which end-users seek to avoid, the nondegenerate locus of a polynomial system needs to be computed. The nondegenerate locus comprises points where the codimension of the solution set matches the number of equations in the system. Historically, the nondegenerate locus has been obtained using ideal-theoretic techniques like saturation ideals and equidimensional decompositions. We propose an algorithm leveraging signature-based features of Gröbner basis algorithms to directly calculate the Gröbner basis for the nondegenerate locus closure without initially solving the entire polynomial system through Gröbner basis computation.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. The results demonstrate that direct photons in Cu$+$Cu collisions exhibit a pronounced enhancement at low momentum and a suppression at high momentum compared to calculations of binary-scaled p$+$p collisions. The data collected suggest a higher-than-expected suppression in Cu$+$Cu collisions at intermediate momentum compared to what was observed in Au$+$Au collisions at the same energy level but with twice the event count. The data are compared to recent theoretical models in both $d+$d and Cu$+$Cu collisions across various energies.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph K4^3 by finding the maximum l1-norm of a K4^3-free n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph's codegree vector. We develop a new method for determining hypergraph extremality and apply it to calculate the asymptotic extremal function of the tetrahedron graph under our novel framework. The codegree squared sum, or co2(G), is introduced to measure codegree magnitude in a 3-uniform hypergraph, with exco2(n,H) representing the maximal codegree squared sum among n-vertex H-free hypergraphs. Utilizing flag algebra computations, we determine the codegree squared extremal numbers for K4^3 and K5^3 and demonstrate associated stability properties, revealing the structural resemblance of extremal K4^3-free hypergraphs to the conjectured extremal hypergraphs of Turan's tetrahedron problem. Additionally, we identify key general characteristics of exco2(n,H), such as the existence of a scaled limit and invariance under vertex size increases.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via alpha operation. Our findings indicate this technique yields a genuine anti-aliasing effect while reducing memory consumption, raising frame rates, and minimizing GPU usage. We tested the proposed method on various maps and found it surpasses or at least matches the performance of existing vector map rendering engines. Our anti-aliasing technique has been openly shared on GitHub to facilitate its application in vector map rendering.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation method based on radial basis functions, which allows for the direct computation of least-squares approximations. The method utilizes the hyperbolic tangent function to calculate distances and exhibits more favorable convergence characteristics than the conventional multiquadric method. The transcendental interpolation framework is ideal for parameter estimation in nonlinear least-squares problems and is particularly well-suited for scenarios where data are influenced by a scale factor or noise with varying intensity.

Pulsar halos are large, bright displays that can be seen in the sky, formed when high-energy electrons interact with magnetic fields. These particles, which make up the halos, come from the rotation of pulsars, and their presence sheds light on how high-energy particles move through the Galaxy's messy environment. By examining the brightest halo, the Vela pulsar's display, researchers have gained new insights into how charged particles at extremely high energies navigate through the Galaxy. This research indicates that, to explain the limited size of the halo, particles must encounter obstacles, like thick clouds of gas, in less time than it takes them to travel a distance equal to the distance between the Earth and the nearest star, other than the Sun. This research has helped scientists understand how high-energy particles move through the Galaxy and has provided new information on the Galaxy's magnetic field.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct characteristics that distinguish different weather conditions.
Existing approaches to this problem are largely confined to specific environments and only tackle the classification of two weather types.
In this study, we introduce the RFS dataset, which includes images representing three categories of weather (rain, snow, and fog), and propose a novel algorithm utilizing super-pixel masks for data augmentation to yield satisfactory results using multiple Convolutional Neural Network configurations.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as evident from our creation of a Climate Change Index for Europe and the US based on media mentions, whereas economists show relatively little interest as measured by prominent journal publications. Interestingly, science journals and policymakers display more consistent interest in the subject.

Soft grippers are increasingly popular across various applications due to their versatility and flexibility, yet accurately modeling and controlling them to grasp objects efficiently remains challenging. Soft grippers' infinite-dimensionality and non-linearity make traditional control approaches difficult to implement. In response, researchers have turned to data-driven methods. However, current methods typically require extensive model updates during execution, hindering real-time control capabilities. In this work, a new data-driven method is proposed that uses dimensionality reduction to create a compact, predictable model, ensuring soft gripper performance can be efficiently controlled in real-time. The main objective is to train the model such that it remains effective across different initial conditions, which is achieved through a training technique involving the simultaneous optimization of both the reduction operator and the rejection of unwanted eigenvalues. Experimental validation of the proposed method was done using a 2D simulation of a soft gripper in contact with a solid surface, proving the method's ability to predict and control the gripper's movement and interaction with the surface.

One of the fundamental problems in science and engineering involves finding the lowest cost value for a given function, known as an optimization problem. Various numerical methods have been proposed to solve this problem, but the Gradient Descent method remains the most popular due to its ease and effectiveness. Nonetheless, this approach is hindered by two major limitations: it often gets stuck in local minimums and has slow convergence rates in some cases. In order to overcome these constraints and accelerate the descent process, a novel method has been developed by introducing a random step element and an accelerated step element, both based on statistical distribution principles. The method exhibits faster convergence and a higher success rate in comparison to the traditional Gradient Descent method, as evidenced by tests on various cost functions.

High-energy emissions from ancient supermassive black holes can provide a direct look into the black hole activity in the early universe. Specifically, misaligned jets of high-redshift active galaxies should make up a significant portion of these distant galaxy populations, but current surveys have only identified a small fraction of these intense jet-producing galaxies. Among these intense jet-producing galaxies, those exhibiting compact symmetric pairs (CSPs) are particularly valuable due to their strict velocity limits, allowing for precise calculation of their luminosity. In a recent search for these intense jet-producing galaxies at even higher redshift, we systematically examined a collection of ancient supermassive black hole candidates, all of which were observed by the Very Large Array and had been listed in the Sample Analysis Survey. Following this search, we reported the sudden discovery of a dense, young galaxy group identified as J1047+6217. Within this new galaxy group, we have now precisely measured the movement of its individual components, revealing two dense spiral galaxies approximately 1.8 billion light-years apart. Further observation of J1047+6217 confirms the presence of extremely intense, high-energy emissions, suggesting that these dense spiral galaxies are actually the source of particularly powerful and concentrated black hole activity. Notably, we have found that these dense spiral galaxies are among the most ancient supermassive black hole candidates with the highest redshift listed in the Sample Analysis Survey, with a redshift of approximately 4.72. This research focuses on improving survival time prediction for lung cancer patients, which, despite significant progress in recent years, still lacks effective solutions. Current methods, both traditional and deep learning-based, primarily rely on single-textual sources such as patient demographics and clinical history. Unlike existing approaches, this study explores the potential of combining multiple data types like text-based clinical information and visual medical scans to inform survival time predictions, simulating the decision-making process of a medical professional. Building on this insight, this work introduces the Lite-ProSENet model, which integrates multiple data modalities and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding an unprecedented 89.3% concordance in predictive accuracy using a public dataset.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning, allowing the agent to efficiently process and generalize from past experiences, avoid unnecessary data, and extract relevant patterns. Natural language can be an effective means of representing the state. This overview discusses the benefits and challenges of employing Natural Language State Representations (NL-SR), highlighting the various ways in which they are used, the techniques employed to learn them, and the areas of study in which they have proven particularly valuable. By exploring the existing literature, we identify the most effective approaches and point out possible avenues for further research.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological density perturbations through observed quasar spectra analysis. By leveraging sophisticated simulations of cosmic structure formation, a substantial synthetic dataset of absorption spectra and associated 1D matter densities is generated. With this dataset, a series of machine learning models are constructed to predict matter density power spectra. We achieve reconstruction accuracy of approximately 1% for certain wavelengths while noting a corresponding error increase at higher wavelengths. Furthermore, we investigate the size of datasets required to attain a specified error rate, highlighting the data requirements for a desired level of accuracy. This work lays the groundwork for analyzing the forthcoming large-scale datasets anticipated with future observational facilities.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to $U(\frak h)$ are one-dimensional over a specific Lie algebra. Subsequently, we establish the conditions under which the irreducibility of a particular module occurs when it is formed through a tensor product of certain other modules. Additionally, we establish connections between certain types of harmonic modules and quasi-finite highest weight modules, before studying the irreducibility of modules composed of tensor products of these types with modules that have a specific module structure.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases from various publishers. We then tested the LSTMs and Convolutional Neural Networks 
from the mainstream computer vision and natural language processing communities to see which
would work best for sentiment analysis. Our study shows that using pre-trained models, 
such as Pre-Trained Transformer models, can be more beneficial than relying on carefully
hand-engineered networks.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue models have achieved significant breakthroughs.
Despite this, developing a scalable chat system poses a major challenge due to
the requirement for substantial human-human dialogue data to support features
like persona, style, or safety. To tackle this issue, our work aims to introduce
role constraints to open-domain dialogue systems that enable them to consistently
maintain assigned roles during human conversations. Achieving this involves
defining a role specification with specific criteria for stated features and
policies on allowed types of utterances. To build this system efficiently, we
propose a framework for collecting data that leverages few-shot learning from
large language models, thereby enabling the creation of role-compliant dialogue
datasets from scratch. Furthermore, we examine various open-domain dialogue
system architectures in terms of their ability to meet role specifications and
maintain natural conversation. Results from both automatic and human evaluations
reveal that our models perform satisfactorily in terms of role conformance, while
still delivering competitive performance on overall conversational metrics.
