The combination of rotating objects and widespread availability of these scenes makes them an ideal platform for the development of highly accurate, real-world 3D object pose estimation models. The proposed method capitalizes on the presence of these rotating points of interest to develop a robust estimation framework, focusing initially on selecting the optimal view and then determining the 3D pose. In contrast to existing models, this approach yields superior 2D-3D alignment results for rotating objects, according to testing conducted on the ObjectNet dataset, and significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in 3D pose estimation, especially in scenarios with limited occlusion.

Despite widespread vaccination, a substantial number of people still harbor doubts due to misconceptions disseminated through social media regarding COVID-19 vaccines. Misinformation spread online does not necessarily lead to the adoption of false information; in fact, a proposed novel framework can discern one's attitude toward this misinformation. This new framework leverages neural networks and attitude consistency to classify stances toward COVID-19 vaccine-related misinformation. A novel neural framework, utilizing knowledge graphs to organize stances, successfully identifies attitudes toward this misinformation with outstanding results, outperforming other current approaches. Experiments were conducted on the recently created CoVaxLies dataset, a comprehensive collection of COVID-19 vaccine-related misinformation gathered from Twitter discussions. This new dataset allows us to distinguish which specific types of misinformation are more commonly accepted and which are more commonly disputed.

Advancements in attosecond science hold great potential to unveil the core electronic behavior of matter, contingent on achieving two interconnected technological milestones linked to high-order harmonic generation sources. Firstly, achieving a higher photon flux would allow researchers to measure even the faintest electronic processes, while also attaining better spectral tunability would grant selectivity in targeting specific electronic transitions. Breakthroughs are made feasible by parametric waveform synthesis, giving scientists the capability to craft controllable, highly-tunable high-energy electric transients. Our findings demonstrate that by manipulating the waveform of the driving laser pulse via its relative phase and carrier-envelope phase, it's possible to exert fine-grained control over attosecond pulse characteristics. This innovation not only amplifies experimental possibilities in the realm of attosecond science, but also paves the way for a highly sophisticated, coherent manipulation of free-electron paths.

Eclipse predictions for binary stars can be complicated by several factors.
These predictions can be affected by a change in the visible star's position 
as the stars orbit, causing the eclipse episodes to recur at different 
intervals: some may repeat at regular intervals, while others may skip or 
be overlooked.
This paper reviews various periodic and non-periodic changes in eclipse 
episodes for binary and multiple-star systems, covering systems where the 
visibility of eclipses is sometimes blocked by other stars in the field 
(viewing eclipses of binary stars as seen from different angles).
A particular emphasis is given to systems where the blocking star's 
position changes gradually: systems where the viewing angle changes 
incrementally due to the stars' motion in their orbits and where the 
eclipse episodes are blocked by other stars occasionally.
A detailed analysis is also conducted on systems where the viewing angle 
changes incrementally: systems considered to be viewed from an ideal angle.

This paper investigates solutions to the Schrödinger equation under the influence of a focusing nonlinearity with mass-supercritical properties, in a domain exterior to a compact convex obstacle in a higher-dimensional space. We demonstrate that solutions with negative energy will inevitably collapse within a finite time period. Additionally, under the assumption that the nonlinearity is not too strongly energy-dependent and given specific symmetry conditions, we establish the same optimal blow-up criterion found by Holmer and Roudenko for solutions in an infinite domain. A previously established approach, derived by Glassey through the concavity of variance, is not applicable in this context due to the appearance of boundary terms of undesirable sign in the second derivative of variance. Our primary argument introduces a new, modified variance measure, bounded by an elliptic operator with positive constant, and is ultimately shown to be nondecreasing. This approach may also be employed to extend the established blow-up criterion to the same symmetry-assumed solutions in an infinite domain.

Physics-informed neural networks offer an innovative solution for partial differential equations that combines adaptability and efficient incorporation of observed data. Despite achieving significant success across a wide array of differential equations, further improvements to computational efficiency are required for this approach. To address this need, enhancing training point generation is an important direction of investigation. Both adaptive and quasi-uniform sampling techniques have previously been explored, each showing benefits. To leverage these insights, we introduce Residual-based Adaptive Node Generation, which combines an adjustable nodal distribution method and a memory mechanism. We then conduct experiments on both linear and nonlinear PDEs, evaluating its accuracy and efficiency relative to traditional sampling methods.

This study examines the behavior and simulation of multi-domain ferroelectric FETs by analyzing the oscillations in their electrostatic conduction band profile, which are characteristic of these devices. We model these dynamics by solving coupled two-dimensional Poisson's equations and energy equations, and find that the system converges to a stable thermodynamic state through energy minimization. Our analysis also shows that the movement of domain walls within the ferroelectric material leads to the negative capacitance effect, which in turn affects the device's drain current and variability due to the domain period. We also investigated how the domain wall's soft or hard state transition influences the device's electrical properties and transport. Our simulations are verified through both experimental data and phase-field modeling.

A significant knowledge gap exists in understanding the Cargo ecosystem's architecture and how vulnerability dissemination occurs within it. Existing studies that generalize security management approaches across multiple ecosystems often overlook the unique technical characteristics of individual ecosystems, hindering direct applicability of security governance strategies to Cargo. To address this disparity, this research employs knowledge graph techniques to construct a dependency vulnerability graph for Cargo and presents an innovative algorithm to identify vulnerability dissemination paths and scope. By conducting a comprehensive empirical study on Cargo's ecosystem, this research investigates vulnerability traits, propagation extent, and factors influencing vulnerability dissemination, revealing that Cargo's security vulnerabilities primarily stem from memory-related issues. Notably, 18% of libraries still harbor vulnerabilities even after 2 years, while 71.6% of Cargo's ecosystem versions are affected by propagated vulnerabilities. This study's findings offer actionable insights for Cargo administrators, developers, and library owners to enhance ecosystem security and presents new concepts for bolstering Cargo's overall security posture.

For analyzing ergodic properties in stochastic dynamical systems, it's essential to demonstrate irreducibility. This paper confirms the irreducibility of stochastic complex Ginzburg-Landau equations subjected to discrete jump noises and shows these results apply universally, imposing minimal restrictions on noise conditions. A critical factor in this study is the authors' and T. Zhang's previously established criteria for irreducibility in stochastic equations with jump noises. This proof is then utilized to demonstrate ergodic behavior in stochastic complex Ginzburg-Landau equations and includes scenarios of weak dissipation with jump degenerate noise.

For a finite noncyclic nilpotent group G, we're analyzing the minimal vertex degree in its power graph. This power graph connects vertices based on one being a positive power of the other. By examining the group's prime divisors and Sylow subgroups, we've pinpointed vertices related to its cyclic subgroups. This allows us to establish a connection between the group's properties and its minimal vertex degree in the power graph. This study provides degree calculations for specific types of noncyclic abelian groups.

Hadron-hadron collisions in the intermediate Feynman-x region (between 0.1 and 0.9) have not been extensively studied at high-energy ranges above sqrt(s) = 63 GeV using the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings. I explore a feasible method to investigate this at the Large Hadron Collider operating at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV, an equivalent increase in fixed-target energy of 40,000 times, with crucial implications for understanding the characteristics of cosmic ray showers.

Deep learning models, specifically Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs), are capable of generating robust image representations, but are limited when dealing with orientation transformations. To address this limitation, we have developed a novel model, Orientation Convolution Networks (OCNs), based on Landmark Gabor Filters (LGFs), which can learn representations that are less sensitive to orientation changes. By combining LGFs with standard DCNNs, our OCNs can leverage the benefits of both Gabor filters and deep learning, while minimizing their respective drawbacks. Through comprehensive experiments on widely used image recognition benchmarks, our OCNs have demonstrated superior performance, with significant improvements over existing DCNNs and previous LGF-based models.

This study seeks to enhance the computational efficiency of graph convolutional networks (GCNs) in point cloud learning. We note that previous GCN optimizations, which relied on pruning techniques, generally decreased the diversity of convolutional operators and thus negatively impacted inductive learning capabilities. To address this limitation, we propose a novel optimization approach that maintains the variety of distinct convolutional operators while simplifying each. This approach involves pruning each operator's parameters while safeguarding its inductive learning potential. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy through thorough evaluations on various point cloud classification and segmentation datasets, including ScanNet and SUN RGB-D. Our optimized method yields a significant computational cost reduction (up to 132x) along with preserved or improved accuracy and a substantial decrease in memory usage.

We introduce a groundbreaking type of Trojan attack, which uses fixed images in conceptual meaning but can take various forms visually. Unlike existing Trojan attacks, which embed inconsequential triggers in clean images, our method considers trigger images as full-resolution representations of meaningful object classes. As our backdoored classifier is designed to recognize the inherent concepts of trigger images rather than specific patterns, it can be triggered by semantically similar images with distinct appearances, making our attack more applicable and resilient to countermeasures in real-world scenarios. Our experiments show that even with limited Trojan patterns, our approach can adapt to new trigger images within the same category and evade sophisticated defense strategies effectively.

We are developing an image slicer for an integral field unit, ROSIE IFU, to integrate up to nine such slices, thereby obtaining multiple tunable near-infrared spectral ranges between 2.28 to 2.4 $\mu$m with a resolution of $R \sim 2000$. This newfully functionalized device, built upon a legacy of work by NITAR, will be installed on the Gemini South telescope and feature a $1.5" \times 7.5"$ field of view. Our study focuses on the optical and thermal performance of the ROSIE IFU, examining the effects of its components, temperature considerations and the environment on which it operates. Our research has led us to conclude that we are on track to meet our specified resolution and can anticipate an on-sky performance that meets 95% of our planned specifications.

In this paper, the carbon-carbon fusion research is revisited to incorporate the latest developments. Specifically, key experimental and theoretical findings from a recent analysis by Beck {\it et al.} (Eur. Phys. J. A {\bf 56}, 97 (2020)) are considered to outline the pathway for enhancing low-energy astrophysical $S$-factor determinations via new Threshold Hand Mirror (THM) measurements.

A crucial aspect of discovering and studying exoplanets is identifying terrestrial planets resembling Earth. New studies emphasize the significance of considering volatile depletion in star composition to predict the bulk composition and internal structures of these planets. In this research, we apply this concept to a sample of 13 stars that host terrestrial planets similar to our Sun, utilising high-precision data on their elemental abundance. Based on this data and simulations of planetary development and volatile loss, we calculate the probable steel-to-silicate mass ratios and volatile contents in the bulk of these planets. Our study reveals wide variability in the composition of these planets, primarily due to differences in their host stars' elements. These calculations predict iron-rich cores and diverse internal structures within these planetary systems, which could lead to interesting interactions between internal heat production and thermal expansion throughout their development.

Deep neural networks can offer flexible and efficient solutions to wireless localization, but their performance depends heavily on high-quality channel state information (CSI). However, collecting and processing raw CSI can be very time-consuming and highly sensitive to noise. Therefore, using raw CSI might not be a practical solution for deployed wireless localization systems. To overcome this limitation, a new approach is introduced that uses a CSI-based attention mechanism to enhance the effectiveness of deep neural networks. By selecting the most relevant CSI components through an encoder-decoder network, the attention mechanism allows the deep neural network to focus on the most important spatial and temporal factors influencing channel responses. As a result, the proposed method offers superior out-of-sample generalization performance compared to traditional deep neural networks using raw CSI. Experiments conducted on a 8x8 element Wi-Fi array demonstrate that this new attention mechanism leads to a substantial 71.9% reduction in training data required for the deep neural network to achieve the same level of accuracy.

This paper presents a comprehensive framework for modal logic semantics by linking different types of logical meaning in the literature to the topological categories theory. Building on similar methods in categorical logic, we will thoroughly examine the relationship between the structural composition of the modal language, its various expansions, and the topological categories, thus offering an abstract understanding of the underlying logical framework.

A graph's edge coloring can be described as assigning different colors to edges based on a specific distance criterion, effectively mirroring the requirements of a certain vertex coloring in a transformed version of the graph. This notion was initially proposed as an open problem by Faudree, Schelp, Gyárfás, and Tuza in 1990, assuming a bipartite graph of high enough girth and a specific degree constraint could be colored using a certain number of colors, but in 2021 this was contested. Now, another example is given which also contests the conjecture originally presented by those authors.

We investigate functions defined on the vertices of the Hamming graphs H(n,q), focusing specifically on those with support contained in the direct sum of the eigenspaces U_i(n,q), U_{i+1}(n,q),..., U_j(n,q) where 0 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ n. Under certain conditions, specifically when n is greater than or equal to the sum of i and j, and when the size of the alphabet is 3 or greater, we identify the functions with minimum possible support and establish a characterization for those with such a minimum. In scenarios where n is less than the sum of i and j, but with a sufficiently large alphabet size of at least 4, we identify similar properties of functions. In particular, we establish a characterization for the functions within the eigenspace U_i(n,q) with minimum possible support in several specific scenarios.

COPASI is a widely-used simulation and analysis tool for biochemical networks and their dynamics, but users had to run it locally as a standalone application. To address this limitation, we developed ShinyCOPASI, a web-based platform allowing users to interact with COPASI models through their web browser. Built with R using CoRC and Shiny, ShinyCOPASI mirrors COPASI's interface for seamless exploration and enables running tasks available in the original software within a browser. It offers a basic model upload feature and a server-loaded model option, providing web access to existing models. Users can access ShinyCOPASI at http://shiny.copasi.org/ and the source code at https://github.com/copasi/shinyCOPASI.

Deep neural networks are fundamentally altering the landscape of how data and physical laws are combined, resolving complex problems in physics and engineering that had proven insurmountable with conventional methods. Nevertheless, evaluating the accuracy of NN-based predictions proves more complicated than traditional methods. This difficulty arises from not only the random fluctuations inherent to noisy data but also the inherent limitations of the data, model misspecifications and imbalances in the training data, all of which are intertwined with uncertainty. This work aims to shed light on the diverse forms of uncertainty that can arise during NN-based inference and potential remedies to mitigate their impact, with a focus on physical systems rather than general applications.

We are investigating quantum group analogues of the free group factors' radial subalgebras, specifically those of class functions, within the context of compact quantum groups. We found that the algebras of class functions for the free orthogonal quantum groups cannot be maximally abundant *-subalgebras (MASAs) under certain conditions. Central to our research is the concept of a quasi-split inclusion. We demonstrated that the inclusion of the class functions' algebra is quasi-split in certain unitary quantum group scenarios. Additionally, we showed that the resulting subalgebra is non-abelian. We obtained new examples of non-abelian radial subalgebras using our findings.

Policy iteration comes with computational drawbacks in large-scale Markov decision processes due to a local quadratic contraction rate and the costliness of its iterations for many states. In response, we introduce a method that allows for the efficient evaluation of policies within these processes. This evaluation method, rooted in the same principles as policy iteration, runs at a speed comparable to value function estimation for these processes. Furthermore, we show that combining this evaluation method with policy iteration results in a algorithm with the same contraction rate as policy iteration but at a speed increased by a factor at most O(\sqrt{S}) over value function estimation. We support our claims with experiments in grid-world domains and a range of additional findings.

Consider a weighted directed graph, denoted as $\mathcal{D}$, and the edge ideal associated with it, labeled as $I(\mathcal{D})$. We establish in this study that the ordinary and symbolic power series of $I(\mathcal{D})$ share the same equivalence for a specific subclass of weighted directed trees. Moreover, the paper also identifies both the minimal generators and Grobner fan of $I(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is a weighted directed tree.

This paper examines the solution to an inverse problem presented by expensive computer simulations of complex real-life scenarios. Specifically, researchers focused on an expensive hydrological model designed to generate realistic data for Athens, Georgia, USA. To efficiently handle the large datasets produced by such simulators, an approach involves first selecting key points to approximate the output, and then applying a specialized method to estimate optimal input parameters at those points, while accounting for any uncertainty in the solution. A comprehensive simulation-based study compares the proposed technique with other established methods on a range of synthetic and real-world scenarios.

Research has shown that certain distributional assumptions are required to guarantee the reliable learnability of complex concepts when evaluating a robust model's accuracy and considering the influence of random example exposure, according to Gourdeau et al. (2019). Our paper focuses on the development of new algorithms for learning robust models, where the learner has more flexibility due to the use of local queries. We create the first algorithms that allow a robust model's training with example influence limited to a fixed radius, even in the presence of label manipulation, while only depending on a flexible assumption and requiring no prior knowledge of the concept boundary. Notably, our models remain nearly accurate when faced with adversarial example influence and maintain a strong distance between similar hypotheses. We introduce the concept of local similarity, which we prove is necessary for robust learning models that take example influence into account. Our first algorithm, designed for the binary classification task, operates by iteratively refining a robust model, where each iteration involves updating the model and its influence radius through a query that identifies potentially similar, yet label-different, regions. Our second algorithm, developed for general classification tasks, works by maintaining a set of models for various, uniformly divided, sub-spaces, where each iteration involves updating the model and its influence radius via a query that identifies a sample from a hard-hat zone. Both algorithms ultimately converge to meet the desired influence criterion, although generalizing them proved challenging due to the requirement for local similarity, which becomes difficult to achieve as the

For the first time, fragmentation functions for jets associated with a lone jet have been measured in collisions involving lead lead and proton proton particles. This specific measurement was made with data from the CMS detector, which operates at a collision energy of 5.02 TeV. Jets, those that originate from a high-energy quark or gluon, are identified within a specific transverse momentum range and are relevant to certain regions within the collision. Fragmentation functions, which represent the distribution of charged particles within a jet, have been found to differ significantly in central collisions of lead lead particles when compared to proton proton particles. However, this difference in fragmentation functions is not seen in collisions occurring at the outer edges of the collision. Additionally, this discrepancy is seen to increase with higher jet transverse momentum, reaching a maximum transverse momentum of one hundred GeV. This increased sensitivity to the effects of the medium when the jet transverse momentum is high, indicates a significant influence of the medium on the fragmentation process, one that goes beyond simple suppression measurements.

Recent research involving Feynman integrals has highlighted the significance of Apéry-type inverse binomial series. Building upon previous findings that non-alternating central binomial series could be solved using level four multiple zeta values, we now show that alternating versions require level eight and can be solved using an alternative approach. This involves the substitution of hyperbolic trigonometric 1-forms for their standard trigonometric counterparts.

Follow-up research on WISEA J153429.75-104303.3, previously reported by Meisner et al in 2020, has yielded an assortment of peculiar attributes for the Y dwarf, 2MASS J1047+0323, revealed through the discovery of its most comparable companion, WISEA J153429.75-104303.3. Several distinctively bright Y dwarfs, notable for their exceptionally bright optical and near-infrared colors, have been discovered using multiple adjacent color indices. Contrasting this, the newly discovered dwarf, reported by Meisner et al, exhibits a peculiar pattern with both upper and lower limits of these color indices in comparison to the aforementioned Y dwarf. According to estimates, the pair is separated by approximately 5.7 pc, making them the closest known pair of Y dwarfs in the solar neighborhood. By analyzing their properties side by side, researchers are gaining insights into the diversity of Y dwarfs. Notably, the pair shares a striking similarity in terms of their spectral energy distributions when graphed against various spectral types. Interestingly, the pair's properties seem to bridge the gap between late Y spectral types and earlier Y spectral types with more typical brown dwarf characteristics. As photometric data continues to improve our understanding of Y dwarfs, it is expected that the discovery of these two dwarf Ys will pave the way for a revised and more precise classification system for Y dwarfs.

The initial production measurement of various particles such as pions, kaons, 
protons and $\phi$ mesons in midrapidity for Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV is
reported. Extracted transverse momentum spectra and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated yields are
analyzed across several centrality intervals spanning from p-Pb to mid-central Pb-Pb
collisions based on final-state particle count. Investigating Xe-Xe and Pb-Pb collisions 
with similar charged-particle counts allows for comparison of initial geometric 
properties and flow behaviour. Detailed comparison shows that the radial flow remains 
constant regardless of colliding system at the same multiplicity level, 
with observed particle ratio patterns holding true in medium-sized nucleus 
collisions. Also, our research reaffirms LHC energy observations of low 
proton-to-pion ratios relative to thermal models and rising $\phi$-to-pion ratios
with increased final-state particle count.

We develop a novel, numerically efficient approach to solving DGLAP equations for single and double parton distribution functions by leveraging Chebyshev interpolation techniques. This method enhances numerical precision with a reduced number of grid points for PDF evolution, achieving improved efficiency. The DPD evolution process utilizes a cost-effective grid-point scheme, enabling the incorporation of two distinct scales for DPD evolution.

Specimens made of Martian and Lunar soil substitutes, in the form of cylinders, were created using a combination of saltwater and heat, and then fired at various temperatures to analyze their internal structure, strength and contraction, which were compared to similar samples made of Earth's soil substitutes. The internal structures of these specimens were studied using a scanning electron microscope, while their mechanical and shrinkage properties were tested through compressive strength and shrinkage rate assessments. The results showed that the optimal firing temperature for these specimens should be around 1100 degrees Celsius, as firing them at lower temperatures led to weaker internal structures and lower strength, due to insufficient sintering, whereas high firing temperatures resulted in more dense internal structures and higher strength, but also significant shrinkage. The specimens fired at 1100 degrees Celsius exhibited a 50% shrinkage, strong internal structures and high strength, making them suitable for 3D printing applications after being mixed with appropriate binders.

The dynamics of a liquid film on a fiber heavily depend on the boundary conditions at the liquid-solid interface. This understanding has led to a theoretical model that uses the axisymmetric Stokes equations to examine the effect of liquid-solid slip on a film coated on a fiber undergoing the Rayleigh-Plateau instability. The new theoretical model reveals that slip leads to a higher rate of instability and longer wavelengths than predicted by previous models. Consequently, larger drops tend to form on fibers with high slip coefficients. The accuracy of the theoretical model is supported by numerical simulations and experimental results from a study conducted by Haefner, et al., published in 2015 in Nature Communications.

By comparing observed and predicted data for a set of 29 galaxies at a specific wavelength, we assess the reliability of star formation rate predictions made by the Prospector framework. Using a machine-learning model trained on a vast dataset comprising 1.72 million galaxies, we find that the forecast for the Brackett-$\gamma$ line is inaccurate and matches the observed trend only at low redshifts below 0.2. This discrepancy arises from the model's inadequate representation of the galaxies' internal structure, which significantly affects the emission of hydrogen recombination lines at higher redshifts. Furthermore, we notice that the Prospector framework's predictions for other hydrogen recombination lines, such as the Brackett-$\alpha$ and Hubble-$\eta$ lines, also deviate from the observed data at higher redshifts. This highlights the importance of incorporating a precise description of the galaxies' internal structure in the analysis of these lines in the future.

This is the first installment of a two-part series. In this initial chapter, we delves into a comprehensive study on the braided auto-equivalences and (semi-simple) local modules defined over the ribbon graph ribbon graph algebra. Furthermore, we establish a detailed classification of these braided auto-equivalences and their corresponding orthogonal squares. Our research has revealed four distinctive exceptional cases alongside one general instance. We then proceed to investigate subgroups within the group of braided auto-equivalences and their corresponding quotient groups. We analyze these groups using both mathematical structure and diagrammatic methods. We also provide detailed examples to accompany our conclusions.

The Fisher-KPP equation, a reaction-diffusion equation, was first introduced by Fisher for modelling allele spread within genetic populations, but also gained applications by Kolmogorov for a broader range of scenarios. Applying an innovative approach for tackling non-linear partial differential equations provides a distinctive approximate solution to the Fisher-KPP equation, which, however, defies initial intuition. Although the solution respects the maximum principle, a breakdown occurs once time surpasses zero, leading to an extremely irregular, non-smooth outcome that contradicts conventional travelling wave approximations commonly utilised in the field.

This work addresses the UbiComp 2021 Challenge presented by Stabilo, aiming to classify handwritten mathematical terms based on time series data from the DigiPen. The challenge involves recognizing mathematical expressions from 15 possible characters written by multiple individuals. To overcome the initial challenge, a data-driven and rule-based method is employed to segment the DigiPen into individual characters. A binary classifier is developed to differentiate between digits (0-9) and non-digits (+, -, *, /, _, ). Nevertheless, the success rate of this classifier is under 50% due to the simplistic nature of the model. To enhance the accuracy, a more complex machine learning model is utilized in conjunction with data augmentation. Although the accuracy reaches 75.6%, the incorporation of augmentation contributes significantly, highlighting the promise of this approach.

This paper introduces an innovative method for duration modelling in statistical parametric speech synthesis by training a recurrent model to generate phone transition probabilities frame-by-frame. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on specific distribution types and mean durations for synthesis, this new approach can model any distribution on non-negative integers. We explore a median-based output generation strategy, which offers advantages such as being more representative, robust to training data irregularities, and enabling incremental synthesis. This method is in line with a broader goal of concurrently modelling durations and acoustic features at a frame-level. Evaluations show that this approach performs comparably to state-of-the-art methods in predicting the median duration of unseen natural speech.

Species distribution analysis can be effectively conducted through occupancy modeling, taking into consideration inaccuracies in species detection data. To address multiple species, states, interactions, false positives, autocorrelation, and data from various sources, various modifications to the fundamental single species occupancy model have been introduced. However, creating high-performance software that can analyze large spatial data sets is still a developing field. A newly developed package, spOccupancy for R, is designed to fit single, multiple species, and combined occupancy models that are sensitive to spatial relationships. Utilizing a Bayesian approach with Pólya-Gamma data augmentation and Gaussian Process neighbor techniques, this package enables efficient model computation even for extensive datasets. spOccupancy provides intuitive functionalities for simulating data, testing models, verifying predictions, evaluating model performance, and validating data residuals. Through comprehensive case studies, the benefits of this package are showcased.

Due to a lack of dermatologists, patients experience long waiting times for dermatologic care. Moreover, studies have shown that general practitioners make fewer accurate diagnoses compared to artificial intelligence. The Skincare project aimed to address this by creating an innovative diagnostic and decision support system in dermatology. It combined the capabilities of interactive machine learning with deep learning to enhance the skills of doctors and augment diagnostic capabilities, particularly in the identification of malignant skin lesions. A baseline model, trained using a large dermatology image dataset (ISIC), delivered outstanding results and demonstrated potential for widespread application, including support for both general practitioners and dermatologists. The project also focused on creating effective communication channels between humans and machines to facilitate machine learning. In essence, the Skincare project sought to integrate human intuition with artificial intelligence, a key component of future cognitive computers that can improve human performance.

To capture the intrinsic variability of type Ia supernovae from limited spectral data, we developed a probabilistic autoencoder that incorporates a Normalizing Flow component after initial training using an Auto-Encoder. The model's two-stage generative architecture can identify a reduced-dimensional representation of SNe Ia, accurately modeling their spectral evolution across wavelength and time directly from data. Introducing a penalty term to address variability correlations and a multi-stage training framework within our physically-parameterized network enabled the separation of intrinsic and extrinsic variability, eliminating the need for magnitude standardization models. The PAE was applied in several tasks to improve cosmological analyses, such as automatically detecting outliers, generating sample spectra consistent with data distribution, and resolving noisy inverse problems to estimate cosmological distances. Notably, we found three intrinsic model parameters yielded the best results, in line with existing research. The PAE achieved an optimal standardization of $0.091 \pm 0.010$ mag for our test sample of SNe Ia, reducing to $0.074 \pm 0.010$ mag when peculiar velocity contributions are removed. The project's code will be made public on GitHub at https://github.com/aguirre-lab/sne_i_a_variability_pa.

A massive neutral gas outflow has been observed in a gravitationally lensed star-forming galaxy. The outflow is visible in a specific OH+ absorption line, which was measured by the ALMA telescope at high spatial resolution. The data also include CO emission, dust, and stellar light. Analysis of the outflow shows that it has different properties than other elements within the galaxy. The mass of the outflow, as estimated from OH+ and CO, is approximately 6.7 billion solar masses. The outflow's properties are best explained by a conical shape. Depending on the inclination angle, the outflow's rate of gas loss and kinetic energy could be quite high. This suggests that the outflow may impact the galaxy's star formation. The outflow may eventually be re-accreted back into the galaxy, but this would depend on various feedback mechanisms. The estimated gas depletion time in the galaxy is around 1-29 million years.

To study the movement of fluid into a swirling, turbulent plume containing heavy particles that sink more slowly than the plume moves, researchers used controlled experiments in a lab setting. The experiments focused on the effects of particle size, density, and the direction in which the plume gains mass, as well as the direction in which the particles move within the plume. The studies showed that when the direction in which the plume gains mass and the direction in which the particles move are opposites, the movement of fluid into the plume increases significantly. The rate of fluid movement increased in direct proportion to the ratio of the particles' gain of mass to the fluid's gain of mass, and this increased rate was independent of particle size. In contrast, when the direction in which the plume gains mass and the direction in which the particles move are the same, adding particles has no effect on fluid movement. The observed increase in fluid movement, which occurs when the direction in which the plume gains mass and the direction in which the particles move are opposites, can be attributed to inertial clustering, a phenomenon where particles move to regions with high turbulence. The increased concentration of particles can cause convective instability in these areas, which affects fluid movement. The observed behavior, which varies based on the direction in which the plume gains mass, can also be attributed to this mechanism. Extending existing theories, which do not take into account the effect of suspended particles moving at speeds different from the fluid's

Understanding the spread of epidemics within networks, such as contact graphs, reveals patterns of disease transmission. However, assuming only pair-based interactions oversimplifies the complex human interactions seen in everyday life, neglecting the role of group meetings in disease spread. By adopting hyperedges to model these interactions, we create more comprehensive models, allowing the transmission rate to depend on the number of infectious contacts a person has. This approach leads us to develop new spectral conditions and study various types of contagion models, considering both the stochastic individual-level model and the mean-field approximation. Numerical examples and the analysis that follows enable the differentiation between inherent disease characteristics and the impact of individual actions. Ultimately, this framework holds potential for a more precise evaluation of vaccine and medication efficacy in the face of pandemic management.

Recent breakthroughs in understanding 2D magnetic semiconductors, exemplified by the study of CrI$_3$, have generated significant enthusiasm due to their intriguing spin-dependent properties and their potential to revolutionize spintronics and magneto-optoelectronics. Through advanced theoretical calculations, researchers investigated the behavior of spin polarization within the prototype ferromagnetic CrI$_3$ bilayer, which has an in-plane magnetization orientation. Their investigation reveals that this ferromagnetic bilayer displays a rich pattern of spin texture within its uppermost valence bands, which arises from two unique spin cants resulting from the interplay of ferromagnetic order with both chirality and electrical polarization. One type of cant is a result of layer stacking asymmetry and valence state polarization, resulting in equivalent canting patterns on both layers. Conversely, the other cant is a consequence of Rashba effect, which in this ferromagnetic case generates oppositely canting spins on adjacent layers within the same electronic state. Additionally, researchers formulated a set of rules governing spin polarization behavior within magnetic crystals based on their magnetic symmetry properties. Lastly, they extended their analysis to other 2D magnetic semiconductors, specifically ferromagnetic MnTe and MnBiI$_2$, which confirms that the spin cants are a universal property of these materials, thereby offering a control parameter for their spin-based quantum properties and functions.

Throughout a solar-type star's lifetime, its rotation undergoes significant changes, following distinct phases. Upon reaching the zero-age main sequence, its overall rotational velocity slows down, adhering to Skumanich's law and making gyrochronology possible. As they age, some solar-type stars may eventually transition out of this braking phase. Additionally, 3D simulations of these stars have identified various differential rotation patterns, characterized by various types, including bipolar, multipolar, and cyclonic circulation patterns, driven by various processes like tidal forces, magnetic fields, and inertial waves, which we will review.

Deep multimodal learning using K-fan deep Boltzmann machines offers a novel approach to combine multiple input sources. This method can learn a common representation using contrastive divergence and is applied to classification, information retrieval, and other related tasks. A significant drawback of traditional two-fan deep Boltzmann machine models lies in their inability to handle complex multimodal input and limited ability to learn a shared representation. This study seeks to address these limitations by developing a K-fan deep structure model capable of learning a common representation shared among multiple modalities. A key contribution of this work is the proposal of two novel score functions, one of which outperforms the current benchmark. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through exhaustive experiments on institutional review board-approved medical image and text data sets, yielding a 97% accuracy rate for lesion detection and a 90% accuracy rate for their corresponding descriptions.

The use of model checking has become increasingly essential in validating the correctness of multi-threaded programs. Traditional unit and functional tests are insufficient due to the hidden nature of race conditions, which can evade detection by these tests. The McMini model checker, which is based on DPOR, has been expanded with a mechanism that enables the declaration of novel, fundamental thread operations through C code. The mechanism enables end-users to define their own thread activation policies, including the handling of spurious wake-ups triggered by condition variables. By allowing users to define their own thread operation models, the McMini model checker becomes a versatile tool for establishing the correctness of multi-threaded programs, including custom thread activation policies, thus broadening the application of model checking beyond the standard POSIX thread model.

The globally predominant messaging app, WhatsApp, boasts a distinct characteristic 
in its closed nature and user-friendly capabilities of transferring multimedia and
large-scale information sharing to groups, which often facilitates the rapid spread 
of anonymous, encrypted messages. However, the direct delivery of messages to user 
phones enabled by WhatsApp, although personal and immediate, can be exploited to 
circulate baseless rumors and fuel misinformation campaigns. Recent elections in 
Brazil and India are notable examples of such abuse, which have led WhatsApp to 
initiate countermeasures like limiting forwarded messages to a single click. Former 
research on detecting misinformation typically focused on text, which poses a challenge 
due to the presence of multimedia content in WhatsApp messages. Therefore, we 
investigate the development of automated systems for recognizing misinformation in 
WhatsApp by gathering human feedback on multimedia content. Our study showcases 
the effectiveness of employing complementary image and text information in identifying 
misinformation through base-line models and highlights the potential for significant 
performance improvement with the incorporation of additional video content evaluation.

We analyze a general branching population where individual lifetimes are independent and identically distributed with arbitrary distributions, and individuals give birth to new ones at random times following a Poisson process independently from each other. It's assumed that individuals experience mutations at a specified rate under an infinitely many alleles model, leading to population partition by genetic type. This gives rise to a frequency spectrum, denoted by $A(k,t)$, which counts the number of family groups of size $k$ in the population at time $t$. The frequency spectrum process represents a type of non-markovian behavior in the population and its study can help understand the correlation between population members' ages and genetic relationships. Using eigenfunction techniques in perturbation theory, we demonstrate the strong convergence of $A(k,t)$ to a stationary distribution and derive the rate of convergence as $kt^{-1/2}$. Furthermore, under specific conditions on the distribution of individual lifetimes, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the frequency spectrum as $t$ approaches infinity.

The primary goal of our spoofing countermeasure system is to identify artificial effects within spoken input that arise from speech synthesis or voice alteration techniques. We achieve this goal by incorporating a specialized, attentive activation function - the attention rectified linear unit (AReLU) - into our end-to-end system. By selectively amplifying key input characteristics and suppressing irrelevant ones, AReLU enables our system to prioritize artifact-related features. Our proposed system was applied to the logical access task using the ASVSpoof2019 dataset and demonstrated improved performance compared to systems utilizing standard, non-adaptive activation functions.

Supergravity, an extension of the Standard Model with local supersymmetry, may offer a way to describe new phenomena beyond our current understanding.  Exploring the cosmic applications of supergravity provides a platform to investigate the potential outcomes of this theoretical framework, which could serve as the low-energy effective theory of superstrings-a potential quantum gravity candidate.  Developing inflationary models in supergravity, however, poses significant challenges stemming primarily from the constraints on scalar potentials and complicated interactions within the framework, as well as the excess degrees of freedom.  Addressing these issues requires navigating the constraints on desirable inflationary paths, moduli stabilization to achieve a stable de-Sitter phase, and ensuring the scalars remain heavy compared to the Hubble scale to facilitate single-field inflation.  Additionally, supergravity predicts several non-renormalizable interactions, rendering it an effective field theory with unknown implications, which may be complemented by an underlying string theory.  Despite these challenges, constructing inflationary models in supergravity remains a viable endeavor that can provide insight into the cosmic landscape as well as the potential outcomes of supergravity, including the cosmic signatures of the modulus fields.

Nonreciprocal optical systems have diverse applications that manipulate the transmission of light based on its propagation direction. This study examines a distinct class of nonreciprocity related to the correlation of photon pairs rather than the transmission of light. An experiment was conducted and supported by theoretical findings, showing that under specific conditions, the correlation of photon pairs is impacted by the direction of propagation in nonreciprocal optical systems. Notably, this phenomenon occurs even when the system's loss and sensitivity to the propagation direction are minimal. This discovery presents a new set of parameters to achieve complete nonreciproosity and opens the door for advanced functionality in quantum and classical communication systems.

Superconducting quantum circuits are emerging as prominent platforms for quantum computing. For practical applications, it is essential to address material flaws causing decoherence. This study employs terahertz Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy to analyze the local dielectric characteristics and carrier concentrations in aluminum resonators on silicon substrates, critical components of superconducting quantum processors. Near-field measurements reveal a significant correlation between local carrier concentrations and dielectric properties, identifying regions with elevated carrier concentrations that cause marked decoherence. A method is developed to mitigate loss by reducing carrier injection through etching of surface features. Near-field measurements followed by resonator tuning demonstrate an approximate 30 times reduction in decoherence, consistent with theoretical expectations. This study showcases the capacity for localized modification of loss mechanisms in planar microresonators, offering a promising approach for enhancing the performance of quantum processors.

We are looking for infinite cardinals $\kappa$ that allow for a division of the real number line $\mathbb R$ into $\kappa$ unique Borel sets. The well-known Hausdorff solution indicates that $\aleph_1$ sets work in one instance. Our research shows, however, that the size range for these divisions can vary extensively, allowing a specific set of natural numbers $A$ with values 0 and 1 included to dictate when $\aleph_n$ sets work in a specific forcing extension. The study is expanded to closed sets and similar results found that show uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ sizes for these divisions are fairly arbitrary.

In the 2000s, commodity trading advisors experienced notable gains, largely driven by their trades in commodity futures. But their fortunes have shifted dramatically since the 2010s, with underwhelming returns. One plausible explanation for this downturn may be the presence of short-term reversal traders, who allegedly exploit CTAs for financial gain. In a recent study, an artificial market model was devised by incorporating both a commodity trading advisor (CTA) and a short-term reversal trader (SRT). The aim was to establish whether these SRTs were detrimental to CTA profitability in the new century. Notably, the research yielded the opposite outcome - in the new millennium, the notional earnings of the commodity trading advisor actually increased.

Identifying the application protocol is a crucial process in network security monitoring that demands a quick and accurate assessment to support detailed inspection. Although pinpointing the application protocol can be challenging, solely relying on static characteristics like port numbers can be insufficient. As a result, advanced and adaptive approaches have been developed for more precise identification. In this research, the mechanisms of dynamic protocol detection in widely used open-source network monitoring tools are examined. Our investigation on HTTP showcases that all evaluated methods are susceptible to evasion tactics, posing significant risks to real-world network surveillance operations. Furthermore, this study reveals a critical flaw in a commonly employed HPXA technique that can be exploited by malicious actors to deceive monitoring systems. To address this vulnerability, a straightforward mitigation method is introduced and proven to be effective, validated through a practical real-world scenario. Our findings highlight the need for the integration of mitigation measures against false positive generation caused by the mentioned HPXA vulnerability. Additionally, this research sheds light on the challenges associated with portable protocol identification methods and proposes a more efficient and adaptable technique, demonstrated by its success in accurately detecting and mitigating RXA and HPXA protocols. To facilitate the integration of our findings, a publicly accessible protocol identification framework is provided for the benefit of network surveillance operators.

Electrostatic gating limits the flow of electrons in integrated circuits. Another potential means of information transport, magnons derived from spin waves in magnetic materials, is difficult to regulate. However, we found that superconducting strips atop thin magnetic films can completely reflect magnons through their magnetic resistance to stray magnetic fields. The significant frequency shifts resulting from this response effectively halt the forward flow of magnons perpendicular to the magnetic field. By positioning two superconducting gates in parallel with the magnetic field, we were able to create a confined magnon system. The added capability to control coherent magnons enables new functionalities in magnonic devices, including reconfigurable logical circuits and stronger connections to other systems of degrees of freedom.

Federated Learning offers a new approach to machine learning, allowing for the training of complex models without compromising user privacy, as sensitive data remains sealed within users' devices. By combining the advantages of cloud computing and distributed machine learning, FL overcomes the limitations of traditional cloud learning, which risks data leakage. Due to the diversity of user devices, FL often faces issues with inconsistent data representations, leading to 'data leakage'. This difficulty is exacerbated in scenarios where the underlying data is highly structured, such as medical images, which demand not only novel models but also adapted data processing pipelines. Our solution to this problem is the development of a new FL framework that accommodates both model and data adjustments, founded on the principles of domain adaptation and federated learning. This innovative framework is inspired by the concept of two-tier neural networks and aims to standardize data representations through shared embeddings, ultimately facilitating efficient FL processes. Our framework is uniquely positioned at the intersection of two areas, dynamic learning-based adaptations, and federated learning, making it especially suited for handling complex structured data. We evaluated our approach's robustness in scenarios with access to partial and biased data, and compared it to standard FL methods, noticing improved performance, increased stability, and significantly reduced training time. Through successful applications in both image classification and semantic segmentation tasks, we have demonstrated the efficacy of this novel FL framework.

A comprehensive theoretical model is offered in this paper for analyzing high-dimensional entangled systems, specifically the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state. Initially, we apply our approach to measure a complete three-photon GHZ state across three dimensions and then extend it to multi-photon systems within higher dimensional settings. In our model, both hyperentanglement of photons and the quantum Fourier transform are employed. The proposed solution will serve as a useful resource for developing high-dimensional quantum computation and communication.

This research paper delves into the problem of uplink cascaded channel estimation in multi-user multiple-input-single-output systems aided by intelligent-reflecting-surfaces operating within the sub-6 GHz frequency range where channel propagation isn't sparse. A high-performance, low-overhead estimation protocol has been developed to minimize reflection power loss without requiring on-off amplitude control. The proposed solution exploits a common structure within the system, significantly reducing pilot transmission overhead by decomposing the complex cascaded channel into separate user-specific and shared variables. The challenge of highly coupled estimation variables is overcome through the use of optimization-based estimation methods utilizing conjugate gradient and block coordinate relaxation techniques. The protocol has been extensively evaluated through numerical simulations in real-world environments, showing considerable improvements over current state-of-the-art solutions in terms of estimation accuracy.

This study analyzes data from an online monitoring system of U.S. local news to explore connections between COVID-19 coverage, regional case counts, and death rates. Using a publicly accessible dataset of over 180,000 articles from over 300 outlets between April 2020 and February 2021, our research reveals significant correlations between local news coverage and pandemic metrics. Notably, we find that areas with higher COVID-19 local news coverage initially saw increased case counts and later increased death rates, suggesting a roughly three-month lag period. As time progresses, the correlation weakens and becomes negative. Through thematic content analysis, our results indicate that the tone of local news coverage during the early stages of the pandemic appears to influence public health outcomes. However, this correlation decreases over time as other news topics, such as the U.S. presidential election, dominate headlines. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between local news coverage and the COVID-19 crisis, demonstrating a dynamic shift in public health-new media interactions over time.

The fundamental ability to count is a prime example of humans' innate capacity for abstract thinking. In this ability, there's typically a notable turning point where children rapidly grasp and master counting techniques. To simulate this cognitive milestone, we developed an AI system through reinforcement learning. By testing this system with the 'give-N' task - where it's given a binary vector and has to pick 'N' items - we discovered that it showed a similar inflection point in learning. Furthermore, our AI, built using the modular network structure known as the ESBN, was able to learn patterns that allowed it to accurately select items outside of its initial training scope, similar to how humans can apply learned concepts beyond what they initially learned.

Bloom filters provide quick approximations of set membership while consuming minimal memory. These filters help engineers prevent time-consuming actions, such as accessing a disk or the network. A potential substitute for Bloom filters is the cuckoo filter, which often needs less storage and processes information faster. A different solution, the Bloomier filter, has been proposed as an expansion of the Bloom filter. A modification to this concept has also been explored, particularly by Dietzfelbinger and Pagh. Their variation of the Bloomier filter can serve approximate membership queries efficiently, though no comprehensive testing of it exists to date. A different filter was developed, the xor filter, as an implementation of their idea, offering more effective efficiency and speeds. Notably, the developed xor filter can surpass both Bloom and cuckoo filters in performance, all while consuming even less storage space than these solutions. A compact variant of the xor filter was also designed (xor+), resulting in storage needs similar to or smaller than already compressed sequences while providing similar speeds to those seen in Bloom filters.

Several key connections between convex geometry and holomorphic line bundles on smooth projective varieties or K\"ahler manifolds are explored. Our investigation focuses on the relationship between positive products and mixed volumes, leading to the definition and examination of a novel addition technique for divisor classes and mixed divisor classes. We establish new geometric inequalities for divisor classes and provide alternative interpretations of classical convex geometry concepts within the framework of algebraic geometry. Specifically, we recontextualize the Alexandrov body construction, Minkowski's existence theorem, demonstrating their analogues with divisorial Zariski decomposition and the duality between the pseudo-effective cone of divisors and the movable cone of curves, respectively.

A new approach aims to derive market trend insights from dynamic price equations, specifically those that describe how future prices converge to optimal values, thereby maximizing trading volume per unit of time. This methodology stands out for its inherent ability to select a suitable time frame, which is automatically identified by analyzing past market activity and determining the state of highest trading efficiency. To facilitate trend analysis, both historical and forecasted price data are considered, with past prices represented by lagging values and forecasted prices represented by advancing values.

This work presents FLVoogd, a refined federated learning technique that allows servers and clients to cooperatively prevent Byzantine attacks while maintaining user anonymity. Specifically, servers utilize DBSCAN with S2PC to cluster the legitimate data majority without acquiring private user data. Concurrently, clients create duplicate models and engage in distance-controlling testing to tailor their local training processes to meet the diverse needs of each cluster. Through this unified approach, servers and clients work in tandem to prevent Byzantine attacks and optimize model development.

We successfully submitted the winning entry to the NeurIPS 2021 - AWS Deepracer challenge, which required developing a self-driving vehicle model that interacts with its environment through action-reward interactions, by utilizing the Unreal Engine-based simulator provided in the competition. The objective of the competition was to create an autonomous driving model that could navigate a track while avoiding obstacles, using only a camera view of the road, through reinforcement learning with fewest possible expert-guided interventions. Our approach involved the use of multiple model-learning strategies, combining them with explicit inverse reinforcement, with explicit reward engineering to promote safe driving behavior, and finally, by fine-tuning a model-driven policy using sparse reinforcement learning. This winning entry showcased the effectiveness of controlled exploration in making learning more efficient, particularly in autonomous driving domains with few guided interventions.

Significant progress in deep learning technology has enabled the creation of more convincingly authentic deepfakes, which have sparked interest across multiple sectors due to their vast potential applications, despite raising serious societal and security risks. This chapter examines the advancements and difficulties in the production and identification of deepfakes, and also explores the potential solutions to improve the resilience of deepfake detection for a broad range of media, such as real-world images and videos. Furthermore, it proposes future research directions for tackling deepfake-related issues.

The identification of sub-Neptune exoplanets receiving irradiance levels similar to Earth's revitalized the prospect of discovering potentially habitable worlds over the coming decade, with some temperate planets potentially harboring liquid water oceans, provided they do not possess massive H2/He envelopes that would cause them to be excessively hot. Characterizing the masses of these envelopes in planets larger than Earth, especially those with masses of 1.7 to 3.5 Earth masses, remains a challenge to assessing their habitability potential. We demonstrate that observable differences exist between the solubility equilibria and thermochemistry of carbon and nitrogen gases in small vs. massive H2 atmospheres, with the requirement for a liquid water ocean and thermal equilibrium being inherently conflicting. Thermochemical recycling of carbon and nitrogen in the massive atmosphere of a temperate exoplanet typically produces CH4 and NH3, while a small atmosphere atop a liquid water ocean would contain CO2 and N2, with the presence of photochemically produced CO and CH4, and reduced NH3 due to dissolution in the ocean. These distinctive atmospheric compositions produce distinctive features in the planet's transmission spectrum, and multiple observations with the James Webb Space Telescope should enable differentiation between sub-Neptune exoplanets with and without massive H2 envelopes, thereby uncovering dozens of potentially habitable planets.

Inspired by the classic discrete-time model of nervous activity proposed by McCulloch and Pitts in 1943, a new continuous-time model, known as the McCulloch-Pitts network (MPN), has been developed for sequence learning in spiking neural networks. This model employs a localized learning rule, in which synaptic weights are adjusted simultaneously for all inputs to an output neuron. The model leverages the asymmetry of connections between binary neurons to effectively learn and memorize multiple temporal patterns of a single neuron, and its ability to efficiently add new patterns to the memory once it is formed. Furthermore, it has been proven that both learning and pattern addition operations can be performed in a finite number of steps, and simulations have confirmed the model's effectiveness in sequence learning, particularly with regard to storing and retrieving long sequences and sequence extension.

This paper reports on the findings from the 2022 ActiveVision Challenge, a benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of Optical Character Recognition (OCR) models. The issue with current OCR models is that they are typically trained on heavily curated datasets which are far removed from the diversity of real-world text instances encountered in robotics and computer vision applications. To address this limitation, the ActiveVision challenge presented a dataset of sawyer robot benchmarks consisting of 16,000+ text samples with corresponding ground truth, along with a robotic platform to gather diverse text data in real-time. The evaluation criterion focused on active learning and domain adaptation, with scores determined by the integration of an OCR model trained from a limited and evolving dataset of robotic experience data. Our winning entry, developed by researchers from NTU, featured a SimpleOCR base model fine-tuned with 1,600,000 synthetic data points from the OCRDB, along with a set of 500 real text instances gathered from the Sawyer robot. With this model, we achieved an accuracy of 62.6% on the WordSup valuation set and 60.6% on the RealUnseen valuation set, showcasing the potential for OCR models to adapt to real-world text instances through active learning.

A specific type of chaos expansions can effectively analyze differential equations with uncertain factors by approximating random equilibrium states associated with such equations. This study integrates principles from validated calculations to provide precise error assessments alongside findings about chaos expansions representing random equilibrium states. This approach also develops a new framework for validated tracking, which entails accurately calculating separate solution branches in parameter-dependent systems and generalizes seamlessly to multi-parameter tracking. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, this research achieves the precise calculation of random equilibrium cycles in the Lorenz system, as well as solution branches and 2-dimensional planes of steady states in the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

The increased use of sensors in industrial settings has led to the widespread collection of high-dimensional data, despite this comes with its own set of difficulties. Notably, gathering a comprehensive set of readings is challenging due to the inherent limitations of sensors and available resources. Moreover, industrial systems often exhibit complex patterns where underlying structures are hidden, making it crucial to identify key factors and develop predictive models. This work aims to address these obstacles by introducing a new filter-based approach that combines dimensionality reduction and anomaly detection, enabling the identification and detection of changes in complex high-dimensional data. Evaluations using simulated and real-world industrial data demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

We have created a detailed analysis of the origins and development of two disrupted galaxies that merged with the Milky Way's outer layers: the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) and Wukong/LMS-1 systems. Our sophisticated computational model, designed to simulate galaxy growth patterns, is based on exponential infall scenarios and allows for reliable fitting of these patterns using timescales like infall periods and cessation epochs. This robust fitting approach, free of biases, has been successfully tested on 1059 proxy stars across the entire model and we are confident that it will greatly aid in understanding the complex history of galaxy interactions within the Local Group. Our analysis of GSE reveals infall timescales of 5.7 billion years for the main mass addition, with a subsequent 3.7 billion-year period of minor star formation fueled by gas reserves, before ultimately shutting off 8.1 billion years ago. In contrast, the Wukong/LMS-1 system experienced more intense star formation over an 8.1 billion-year period following initial mass addition. Our fitted parameters, coupled with precise metallicity measurements at key inflection points, provide a comprehensive framework for further exploring the chemical and dynamical history of these galaxies and their subsequent merger into the Milky Way.

Given a profinite group G, an S[[G]]-module is a G-spectrum that fulfills certain criteria, leading to the definition of the homotopy orbit spectrum X_{hG} associated with an S[[G]]-module X. When X's constituents meet specific finiteness criteria, a homotopy orbit spectral sequence arises with an E2-term being the continuous homology of G, taking coefficients from the graded profinite \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}[[G]]-module \pi_*(X). This is demonstrated with an equivalence for certain conditions on G and Z: specifically, (Z[[G]])_{hG} is shown to be equivalent to Z in those scenarios, with supplementary methods for further investigation provided.

A major challenge in creating AI models that can automatically process and analyze visually complex documents such as invoices is acquiring a large, high-quality dataset to train these models. Our proposed approach, known as Selective Labeling, streamlines the labeling process by limiting the labels to simple "accept/reject" confirmations for model predictions made on partially annotated documents. This is paired with a specialized strategy for active learning, designed to identify and target model predictions with the highest levels of uncertainty. Our experiments on multiple document types across three different fields have shown that selective labeling can cut labeling costs by tenfold, without a noticeable decline in accuracy.

The EuS/InAs interface has gained attention due to its potential to introduce magnetic properties in a semiconductor material crucial for the development of quantum devices. Using a computational model that incorporates machine-learned data and density functional theory, we have studied how varying the bonding configuration at the interface impacts the electronic properties. Across the examined configurations, we observed that the energy levels at the interface in InAs are positioned higher than those in EuS. Furthermore, we discovered novel states that arise from the interaction between the two materials, and are localized at the interface due to charge transfer. The arrangement of atoms at the interface significantly influences both the energy position and distribution of these states. While an induced magnetic effect is evident in InAs, the magnetic moment is relatively weak.

A comprehensive classification system for subsets of Baire space, categorized by Borel Wadge classes, has been introduced with enhanced effectiveness. Based on Montalbán's true stage machinery, we leverage this innovation to offer an alternative demonstration of Louveau and Saint-Raymond's separation theorem. This leads to a demonstration of Borel Wadge determinacy within the $\text{ATR}_0+\Pi^1_1$-I system of second-order arithmetic.

Deep, wide, and complex Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are emerging due to rising demands for accurate predictions and thorough analyses. However, they necessitate a considerable amount of computational power and time for processing. Previous studies on pruning have focused on enhancing inference efficiency, but there's been limited research on effectively decreasing training costs. Our proposed framework, ClickTrain, efficiently and accurately enables both end-to-end training and model pruning for CNNs, distinguishing itself from previous work with fine-grained architecture preservation through pattern-based pruning, precise weight estimation, and compiler-optimized calculations. As a result, ClickTrain can deploy high-accuracy and fast-pruned models directly without additional overhead compared to traditional methods, while also minimizing the pruning-after-training approach by up to 2.3 times with similar results and up to 2.3 times with the pruning-during-training approach with both higher accuracy and compression ratios, all under equivalent time constraints.

This research examines the specific type of modal lattice derived from bounded distributive residuated lattices with a focus on their modal lattice structure. Specifically, it investigates the way modal lattice extensions relate to the original structure in question. As a result, it identifies a particular class of modal lattices that are consistent and complete.

The collaborations of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory and Virgo have observed the full spectrum of merging compact binaries' gravitational waves. These observations have been categorized into three main types: those resulting from the final merging of two mass objects (binary black holes and binary neutrons), and those that lead to the formation of two or more isolated black holes or neutrons due to the collision's instability. Further research into these detection data has revealed new discoveries, such as the possibility of certain stars being part-solid, fluid, or composed of both (fluid-core and part-solid-core), as well as the likely existence of neutron stars composed of deformed nucleons. Next, we explore the potential for detecting the gravitational waves produced by the breakdown of symmetry in the interior of compact objects, and how these bursts could inform us about the properties of ultracompact objects. Lastly, we discuss the possibilities of detecting gravitational waves produced during the process of compact objects' dielectric breakdown, and how these detections might lead to a better understanding of the upper limits of objects' densities.

A group of researchers conducted a comprehensive study by employing a statistical approach across the entire Kepler field, focusing on metallicity's impact on the habitability of planets within metal-poor star systems.  To achieve this, they first gathered a sample of metallicity values for nearly 300,000 low-metallicity stars, and then made comparisons with the distribution of planets on systems with higher metal content.  Finding significantly fewer Earth-sized planets on low-metallicity stars than expected, the researchers discovered a notable trend: as host stars' metallicity increases, so does the presence of giant planets, and, to a lesser extent, Earth-sized planets.  Utilizing the results to form an analytic prediction for planet formation, the team found that for low-metallicity stars, the presence of Earth-sized planets is greatly reduced, and as metallicity increases, the presence of giant planets peaks at a specific point before stabilizing.  In a related investigation, the team explored the presence of white dwarfs with metal-rich planetary systems, and found that approximately 4.2% of these stars are surrounded by planets within the habitable zone, and a larger fraction by our estimates.

Sequential decision-making in operations management problems, such as those governed by constraints, can be addressed through the lens of constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs). Traditionally, solving CMDPs for optimal policies involves relaxing the problem into a subgradient optimization task, with each iteration introducing an optimal policy for a relaxed version of the problem. Ultimately, this approach yields a policy that achieves a limited return, as it is based on a series of approximations. In contrast, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving a specific type of CMDP - a modified version of the multi-arm budget problem - without resorting to these approximations. Our method guarantees that the resulting policy will not exceed the allowed return and may even achieve the optimal return in some situations.

This research outlines a method for recognizing handwritten mathematical symbols when not using an actual input device, offline. The approach involves segmenting symbols accurately into over 300 categories. Since many complex mathematical symbols require both horizontal and vertical projection to be split, but certain symbols, like the square root symbol, can't be processed this way. What's more, handwritten mathematical symbols can look very similar, for example, handwritten zero and the Greek letter null. Given the numerous mathematical symbols, over 300 in total, a highly effective classifier capable of recognizing such a wide range of symbols must be developed. Initially, this study addressed the challenge of segmentation by applying the Simple Linear Iterative Clustering method. Results showed that the accuracy of the designed neural network classifier for the recognition task was 78% overall, across 305 mathematical symbol classes.

A geometric interpretation is provided for superconformal quantum mechanics based on a hyper-Kahler cone that has a symplectic resolution with equivariant symplectic properties.
